title: K Closest Points to Origin
summary: Return the k input points nearest to the origin.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ number of points ≤ 10,000. Each coordinate is an integer in [−10,000, 10,000]. The selected multiset is unique.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare the multiset of coordinate pairs, including multiplicities. Output order is free.

statement: Return the k input points nearest to the origin. A point is represented as [x, y]. The returned points may appear in any order, and repeated coordinates count with their original multiplicity.

examples.explanation: Their squared distances are 2 and 4, below 17.
Both copies of the nearer point belong in the result.

constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ number of points ≤ 10,000. Each coordinate is an integer in [−10,000, 10,000]. The selected multiset is unique.
hints: Conceptual: Comparing squared distances gives the same order as comparing distances.
Directional: Keep the best k candidates with their squared distances as priorities.
Implementation: Keep the worst retained point accessible. Replace it when a strictly closer candidate arrives, then output the retained points.
complexityAnalysis: O(n log(k+1)) time and O(k) auxiliary space with a bounded max heap.
